## Purpose
`useArtifactDrift.ts`, `useEconomySummary.ts` and `useFileContent.ts` show the three shapes a dashboard hook takes: a single-entity `useQuery`, a per-project fan-out via `useQueries`, and (in `useArtifactDrift.ts`) both in the same file for a primary hook plus a small companion hook. Every one of the three imports its fetcher from a `lib/*` wrapper (never calls `call()` directly, matching the dashboard guard) and every `queryKey` is a stable array literal with the identifying params (`repoPath`, `scope`, `relPath`) as trailing leaves.

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 20
Files are named `use<Noun>.ts`, one primary export per file (the file's namesake hook), with a JSDoc block above it explaining what it fetches, why it's `enabled`-gated, and any live-refresh contract (watcher invalidation vs. `refetchInterval`). All three exemplars gate `enabled` on the nullable identity param(s) (`!!scope`, `!!repoPath && !!relPath`) rather than letting `queryFn` run with an unready value, and all three set an explicit `staleTime`. `useArtifactDrift.ts` additionally derives a plain returned object/map from the raw `useQueries` results (`Record<string, Row>`) rather than exposing the raw TanStack result array to callers.

## How to apply
A new hook goes in its own `src/hooks/use<Noun>.ts` file. Pick `useQuery` for a single entity keyed by one or two stable params, or the `useQueries` fan-out (see `useArtifactDrift`/`useWorkspaceSummary`) when the same fetch must run once per project/row — key each per-item query on the item's own identity (`p.path`), never the array index. Import the fetcher from the matching `lib/*.ts` wrapper; do not inline a `call()`/`fetch` in the hook. Export a `Row`/summary interface next to the hook when callers need a typed shape richer than the raw query result (as `ArtifactDriftRow` does).
